section_summary: This section contains U.S. State Department, FBI, FCC, and diplomatic records from 1942 to 1949 regarding alleged Japanese espionage, propaganda, and subversive activities in Mexico. Key matters include investigations into the Academia de la Lengua Japonesa in Tacubaya, false press reports of clandestine Japanese radio transmissions in Los Mochis, an interview with Benjamin Sutton concerning German and Japanese espionage contacts, and accusations against the Unión Nacional Sinarquista of selling Mexican defense plans. Later documents address legal obstacles and eventual arrangements for the deportation and transit of interned Japanese national Masao Imuro Ota from Mexico to Japan via the United States.

subfiles.about: Cover letter transmitting an FBI memorandum regarding an unlicensed Japanese school in Mexico City.
subfiles.summary: Hoover transmits a memorandum concerning allegations of propaganda at the Academia de la Lengua Japonesa in Tacubaya.
subfiles.title: Letter from J. Edgar Hoover to Frederick B. Lyon regarding Academia de la Lengua Japonesa

subfiles.about: Investigative report on the background, directors, and activities of the Academia de la Lengua Japonesa in Mexico.
subfiles.summary: Details the school's origins, director Yoshi Chika Yoshida's nationalist ideology, conflict with Dr. Kiso Tsuru, and tax status.
subfiles.title: Memorandum regarding Academia de la Lengua Japonesa

subfiles.about: Inquiry regarding a Mexican newspaper report about Japanese spies and a radio transmitter in Los Mochis.
subfiles.summary: Sterling quotes an Excelsior report regarding Japanese spies arrested in Los Mochis and requests Embassy verification and technical details.
subfiles.title: Letter from G. E. Sterling to Clifton P. English regarding Alleged Espionage Group in Los Mochis

subfiles.about: Instruction directing the Embassy to investigate press reports of Japanese espionage in Los Mochis.
subfiles.summary: The Department instructs the Embassy to determine the accuracy of the Excelsior story and report any radio frequencies used.
subfiles.title: Draft Telegram to American Embassy, Mexico City

subfiles.about: Response conveying the Embassy's findings regarding the alleged Japanese spy transmitter in Los Mochis.
subfiles.summary: English encloses paraphrases of diplomatic telegrams confirming that the Excelsior newspaper story was erroneous.
subfiles.title: Letter from Clifton P. English to G. E. Sterling

subfiles.about: Paraphrased text of outgoing telegram requesting investigation of the Los Mochis espionage report.
subfiles.summary: Requests a complete report on the Excelsior story and technical transmission information if verified.
subfiles.title: Paraphrase of Telegram Sent to American Embassy, Mexico City (No. 459)

subfiles.about: Paraphrased text of incoming telegram refuting the Los Mochis espionage report.
subfiles.summary: States that the Excelsior story is completely false and no radio transmitter was found.
subfiles.title: Paraphrase of Telegram Received from American Embassy, Mexico City (No. 288)

subfiles.about: Official telegram confirming that the press story of a clandestine radio transmitter was erroneous.
subfiles.summary: Messersmith reports that the Excelsior story is erroneous, no transmitter was located, and Mexican authorities took no action.
subfiles.title: Telegram from George S. Messersmith to Secretary of State (No. 288)

subfiles.about: Cover letter transmitting an FBI memorandum on the investigation into the alleged radio in Los Mochis.
subfiles.summary: Hoover transmits a memorandum detailing the investigation that disproved the presence of a Japanese radio transmitter in Los Mochis.
subfiles.title: Letter from J. Edgar Hoover to Frederick B. Lyon regarding Los Mochis Investigation

subfiles.about: Investigative report determining the alleged radio transmitter was medical electrotherapy equipment.
subfiles.summary: Details how Pedro Ramirez falsely identified an old medical electrotherapy device in Teramoto's abandoned plant as a clandestine transmitter.
subfiles.title: Memorandum regarding Japanese Radio Station at Los Mochis, Sinaloa, Mexico

subfiles.about: Cover letter transmitting Sutton's signed statement regarding German and Japanese espionage contacts.
subfiles.summary: Hoover transmits Sutton's statement taken after German agent Josef Hermkes named him as a proposed Mexican contact.
subfiles.title: Letter from J. Edgar Hoover to Frederick B. Lyon regarding John Redondo Benjamin Dominic Sutton

subfiles.about: Duplicate copy of Hoover's transmittal letter regarding Benjamin Sutton.
subfiles.summary: Duplicate file copy of Hoover's letter transmitting Benjamin Sutton's voluntary statement.
subfiles.title: Duplicate Letter from J. Edgar Hoover to Frederick B. Lyon regarding John Redondo Benjamin Dominic Sutton

subfiles.about: Voluntary sworn statement detailing Sutton's military background, Mexican activities, travels, and foreign contacts.
subfiles.summary: Sutton recounts his West Point career, Mexican connections, travel to Japan and the Philippines, and contacts with Colonel Nishi and German agents, denying espionage.
subfiles.title: Statement of John Redondo Benjamin Dominic Sutton (Brant)

subfiles.about: Routing note directing that a confidential letter to Ambassador Messersmith be sent by courier.
subfiles.summary: Bonsal instructs that the confidential letter to Ambassador Messersmith be dispatched by courier.
subfiles.title: Routing Slip regarding Letter to Ambassador Messersmith

subfiles.about: Confidential letter advising against Mexican intervention and opposing the repatriation of a suspect.
subfiles.summary: Bonsal agrees not to approach Mexican authorities and notes security agencies will prevent the suspect's repatriation.
subfiles.title: Letter from Philip W. Bonsal to George S. Messersmith

subfiles.about: Duplicate carbon copy of Bonsal's confidential letter to Ambassador Messersmith.
subfiles.summary: Carbon copy of Bonsal's letter regarding national security agencies handling a suspect's repatriation.
subfiles.title: Duplicate Letter from Philip W. Bonsal to George S. Messersmith

subfiles.about: Diplomatic despatch reporting accusations that the Sinarquistas sold Mexican defense plans to Japan.
subfiles.summary: Ray transmits press reports of Deputy Ochoa Renteria's accusation that the Unión Nacional Sinarquista committed treason by supplying defense plans to Japan.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 27311 from American Embassy, Mexico City to Secretary of State

subfiles.about: Press report on demands to close Sinarquista offices over alleged espionage in Baja California.
subfiles.summary: Reports Ochoa Renteria's claim that the Maria Auxiliadora colony betrayed Magdalena Bay defense plans to Japan.
subfiles.title: Newspaper Clipping from La Prensa: Nuevamente se Pide Cierren las Oficinas Sinarquistas

subfiles.about: Press report on accusations by the Defense Committee of the Mexican Revolution against Sinarquistas.
subfiles.summary: Reports allegations that Mexican Squadron 201 pilots found Mexican coastal defense plans in Japanese possession.
subfiles.title: Newspaper Clipping from El Popular: Piden la Clausura de las Ofnas. de la Union Sinarquista

subfiles.about: Press report on Ochoa Renteria's petition to dissolve the Sinarquista organization for treason.
subfiles.summary: Details charges that Sinarquistas supplied Japanese forces with defense plans for Baja California and Magdalena Bay.
subfiles.title: Newspaper Clipping from El Nacional: Seria Acusación a los Sinarquistas

subfiles.about: Despatch transmitting Mexico's request for U.S. assistance in deporting Masao Imuro Ota to Japan.
subfiles.summary: Geist quotes a Mexican Foreign Office note requesting U.S. cooperation to transit and deport undesirable Japanese internee Masao Imuro Ota to Japan.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 1284 from American Embassy, Mexico City to Secretary of State

subfiles.about: Diplomatic instruction detailing legal impediments to transiting involuntary alien deportees through the United States.
subfiles.summary: Instructs the mission to decline Mexican assistance based on Circuit Court rulings that aliens cannot be involuntarily transited for deportation.
subfiles.title: Instruction No. 407 to American Mission, Mexico City

subfiles.about: Legal advice on amending the draft instruction concerning alien deportation transit laws.
subfiles.summary: Diven suggests explaining that U.S. transit laws cover only voluntary transit and habeas corpus prevents involuntary alien deportation.
subfiles.title: Memorandum from F. M. Diven to H. H. Gosho

subfiles.about: Headnotes of Circuit Court decision on the non-deportability of aliens brought to the U.S. involuntarily.
subfiles.from: Circuit Court of Appeals, Second Circuit
subfiles.summary: Summarizes the appellate ruling that an alien brought involuntarily into the United States cannot be deported as an immigrant.
subfiles.title: Legal Headnotes: United States ex rel. Paetau v. Watkins

subfiles.about: Headnotes of Circuit Court decision regarding involuntary entry and deportability of enemy aliens.
subfiles.from: Circuit Court of Appeals, Second Circuit
subfiles.summary: Summarizes the ruling that an enemy alien brought to the U.S. under guard is not deportable as an immigrant.
subfiles.title: Legal Headnotes: United States ex rel. Ludwig v. Watkins

subfiles.about: Internal memorandum urging facilitation of Masao Imuro Ota's deportation in reciprocity for Mexican wartime cooperation.
subfiles.summary: Reveley urges assisting Mexico with Ota's deportation, citing Mexico's wartime cooperation in facilitating deportations of Germans.
subfiles.title: Memorandum from Paul J. Reveley to Gerald A. Mokma

subfiles.about: Personal letter reporting Mexican urgency regarding the deportation of Masao Imuro Ota.
subfiles.summary: Geist informs Reveley that Lic. Sauto is very anxious to expedite the deportation decision regarding Masao Imuro Ota.
subfiles.title: Letter from Raymond H. Geist to Paul J. Reveley

subfiles.about: Transmittal slip forwarding the translated Mexican Embassy note concerning Masao Imuro Ota.
subfiles.summary: Vaillink forwards a translated Mexican Embassy note regarding Masao Imuro Ota to Hughes for handling.
subfiles.title: Memorandum from G. Vaillink to R. L. Hughes

subfiles.about: English translation of Mexican note regarding Masao Imuro Ota's voluntary transit and assassination threat.
subfiles.summary: Reports Ota's voluntary transit waiver and explains Mexico's urgency because he previously threatened the U.S. President's life.
subfiles.title: Translation of Diplomatic Note No. 747 from Mexican Embassy, Washington, D.C.

subfiles.about: Original Spanish diplomatic note requesting U.S. cooperation in the repatriation of Masao Imuro Ota.
subfiles.summary: Official Spanish text requesting U.S. transit cooperation, citing Ota's voluntary declaration and wartime threat against the U.S. President.
subfiles.title: Diplomatic Note No. 747 from Mexican Embassy, Washington, D.C.

subfiles.about: Inquiry to U.S. Political Adviser in Tokyo regarding Japan's admission of Masao Imuro Ota.
subfiles.summary: Outlines INS parole conditions for Ota's transit and asks whether authorities in Japan will admit him.
subfiles.title: Telegram A-46 to U.S. POLAD, Tokyo

subfiles.about: Administrative form marking a replacement record copy for filing in Department records.
subfiles.summary: Administrative sheet designating a replacement record copy for an unreturned action copy to be filed in DC/R.
subfiles.title: Replacement Record Copy Sheet (Form DS-184)

subfiles.about: Telegram confirming no objection to Masao Imuro Ota's entry into Japan as a repatriate.
subfiles.summary: Sebald reports no objection to Ota entering Japan, provided proof of Japanese nationality is presented at port of entry.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 113 from U.S. POLAD, Tokyo to Secretary of State
